title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana + logs for Private installs (Helm + Terraform + upgrade tooling)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments currently lack a one-click observability bootstrap. Customers installing Redwood Private must stitch together Prometheus/Grafana, log shipping, dashboards and alert rules across Helm and Terraform which leads to inconsistent installs and manual post-install steps. This PR adds opinionated automation for observability in private installs: - Helm chart for observability (Prometheus Operator, Grafana, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter) with values tuned for private clusters and resource constraints. - Terraform module to provision Prometheus/Grafana namespaces, persistent volumes (when enabled), and to wire in DNS/K8s RBAC required by the installer. - Fluent Bit & Vector log shipping templates to forward application and platform logs to customer-configured sinks (S3/HTTP/Elasticsearch) with sensible defaults and parsers. - A set of curated Grafana dashboards for inference runtime: per-model latency/throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, request routing splits, and per-tenant token cost breakdown. - Alerting rules for critical SLOs (control-plane API failure, scrape failures, high error-rate for serving replicas, disk pressure). - Upgrade & rollback helpers: helm upgrade hooks, pre-flight checks, and a scripts/upgrade-observability.sh which uses Terraform plan/apply with a dry-run flag and Helm diff checks. Checklist: - [x] Helm chart added under charts/observability - [x] Terraform module under terraform/modules/observability - [x] Installer integration: installer/helm-values and templates - [x] Grafana dashboards JSON and provisioning configs - [x] Alert rules + Prometheus recording rules - [x] E2E smoke test for Prometheus/Grafana scrape and a sample dashboard panel - [x] Documentation: docs/private/observability.md - [x] CI jobs to lint charts and terraform fmt/validate Notes: - This is intentionally opinionated: defaults are conservative (no persistent PVs unless enabled, limited scrape intervals) to be suitable for air-gapped and resource-constrained on-prem installs. - Sensitive values (push endpoints, credentials) are read from user-provided secret refs; installer will surface templated values in the private control plane. - Lifted some existing dashboards from hosted observability and adapted panels to use the operator metrics names used in private clusters. Related: ENG-3245 (observability baseline for private installs), ENG-4012 (installer terraform refactor).

review_comments: Miguel Ramos: Left a few comments on prometheus rules — prefer recording rules for high-cardinality metrics to avoid query slowness.
Asha Patel: Addressed recording rules and added comments explaining cardinality tradeoffs (see prometheus/rules/recording_rules.yaml).
Linnea Chen: Can we avoid creating PVs by default? Suggest keeping persistentVolumes.enabled=false and documenting when customers should enable them.
Asha Patel: Yes, default is false. Added docs section explaining persistent storage implications for dashboards and long-term metric retention.
Samir Gupta: CI failed on first run due to helm lint for chart dependencies. Fixed Chart.yaml and bumped kube-prometheus-stack dependency to a compatible patch version.
CI: helm-diff check initially failed on rename of prometheusRule resources — updated helm hooks to use stable names to avoid resource recreation.
Miguel Ramos: Approved after the recording rules and PV default change. Linnea approved conditional on docs update. Samir approved the installer wiring changes.
ci_summary: Initial CI: failed helm lint (fixed), terraform fmt errors (fixed), helm diff warning (tuned). Final CI: all checks passing. Added smoke e2e that runs in --short mode on PRs and full run in release pipeline.
release_notes: Adds automated observability bootstrap for Private installs: Helm chart (Prometheus/Grafana), Terraform module, log shipping templates, curated dashboards, and upgrade/rollback helpers. Defaults are conservative for on-prem installs. See docs/private/observability.md for install and upgrade instructions.
testing_notes: E2E smoke test verifies Prometheus scrape of node-exporter and kube-state-metrics, Grafana provisioning of dashboards, and a sample alert firing simulated via a test target. Manual upgrade tested on a local k3s cluster (helm upgrade + terraform apply with dry-run).
backout_plan: If issues occur after deployment: 1) Run scripts/upgrade-observability.sh rollback which executes helm rollback and terraform apply with previous state. 2) Disable provisioning via installer flags and re-run installer to remove observability components. 3) Escalate to SRE with collected logs and prometheus snapshots.
notes_for_ops: - For air-gapped installs ensure charts and dashboard JSON are bundled in the private installer bundle. - If persistent metrics are desired enable terraform module persistent_volumes and set retention in prometheus values. - Customers can opt out of log shipping by setting logging.enabled=false in observability values.
security_considerations: Secrets for external sinks must be provided as K8s secrets; the installer does not embed credentials. RBAC roles created are minimal and scoped to the observability namespace. Documented in docs/private/observability.md.
changelog_entry: observability: private install automation (helm, terraform, dashboards, alerts)
notes: This PR consolidates prior experimental work from feature branches and should be the base for future improvements to retention and multi-tenant scraping policies.
